Question Choices: Find the smallest positive integer x such that 5x ≡ 1 (mod 11).
Hints: Try 5×1, 5×2, ... until you get 1 more than a multiple of 11

Question Choices: Find all moduli n > 7 such that 4 and 7 are inverses (mod n), i.e. 4 × 7 ≡ 1 (mod n). List them separated by commas.
Hints: 4 × 7 - 1 must be a multiple of n;n must be larger than 7
Solution: 4 × 7 = 28, so n must divide 28 - 1 = 27 and n > 7. The factors of 27 greater than 7 are 9 and 27.

Question Choices: Find the inverse of 6 (mod 8), or say that it does not exist.
Hints: An inverse exists only when the number and the modulus are coprime
Solution: Does not exist: gcd(6, 8) = 2, so 6 and 8 are not coprime and 6 has no inverse mod 8.
